author: Akien
prose: Imma use an example, the paths may not be correct to the letter, but the idea is the important part, not the path... devices/webserver/groundloop/pulse.py will be our webserver's shim's pulse. so i'm the group loop and i am already running and i look in that folder. last time i was here, pulse.py did not exist. so inside a try/except i can either run it, or i can import it. either way, once i activeate it, it's now in my list of things i know about.... next pass thru, the file is missing. so i remove it from my list. if i imported it, i now unload it. this is true for every device. a goundloop folder can exist at the class level or the instance level. nobody has to do anything except put the file there or remove it. so this keeps the ground loop from needing a restart, from getting stale, from anybody needing to do anything other than just use the provided service or not.
